2607.13408.title: Improving Text-to-Audio Instruction Following via Fine-Grained Feedback from Audio-Aware Large Language Models
2607.13408.paper_summary: Recent text-to-audio models generate high-quality audio, but often fail to follow instructions involving multiple sound events and temporal order. This gap arises because existing evaluation and training signals mainly emphasize global similarity or perceptual quality, with limited supervision on instruction-level correctness. We propose an instruction-level framework that uses audio-aware large language models (ALLMs) as fine-grained judges to verify target event presence and temporal relations in generated audio. After validating ALLM judgments on benchmarks and through human verification, we use their feedback to construct preference pairs for direct preference optimization. We further introduce S3Bench, a narrative benchmark for evaluating multi-event temporal instruction following. Experiments show that our method improves event completeness, temporal ordering, and joint instruction-following accuracy across existing benchmarks and S3Bench, while maintaining audio quality.
2607.13408.paper_summary_zh: 最近的文本到音頻模型生成高品質的音頻，但通常無法遵循涉及多個聲音事件和時間順序的指示。這一差距產生的原因是現有的評估和訓練信號主要強調全局相似性或感知質量，對指示層級的正確性監督有限。我們提出了一個指示層級的框架，利用音頻感知的大型語言模型（ALLMs）作為細緻的評判者，以驗證生成音頻中目標事件的存在和時間關係。在基準測試和通過人工驗證驗證ALLM判斷後，我們利用它們的反饋構建偏好對以進行直接偏好優化。我們進一步介紹S3Bench，一個用於評估多事件時間指示跟隨的敘事基準。實驗表明，我們的方法在現有基準和S3Bench中改善了事件完整性、時間排序和聯合指示跟隨的準確性，同時保持音頻質量。
